note: A direct mesh of measured cloud-top stereo heights in a 64 km aperture near the eruption, from NASA nominal 04:30 UTC retrievals (actual line observation times about 04:36–04:37 UTC) on 15 January 2022. Only native neighboring retrieval pixels with quality rating at least 1 are connected; missing or low-confidence pixels remain holes. All 449 retained observations are also shown as point markers at their measured positions; marker size is a visibility symbol, not a droplet size. The selected source reaches 58.357 km, without height correction or vertical exaggeration. The lower separate surface is historical NOAA ETOPO1 ocean bathymetry at geographic scale, not a post-eruption seafloor survey. Cloud-top brightness uses the co-recorded Himawari-8 infrared brightness temperature, not true-color imagery. This is the observed upper surface at one time, not a reconstructed plume volume, density, eruption column or full umbrella-cloud extent. No stem, skirts, sides or particles are invented. No crop walls, underside, stand, independent ruler or schematic geometry is included. Kristopher Bedka and Konstantin Khlopenkov, NASA Langley Research Center; GOES-17/Himawari-8 stereo retrievals, 15 January 2022; NOAA ETOPO1 ocean-floor elevations.
